items.question: What’s the typical contract length?
items.answer: Most contracts range from 4 weeks to 3 months, with opportunities to extend.

items.question: Do I need experience in remote placements?
items.answer: Experience in rural or isolated locations is preferred but not required. We provide relocation support.

items.question: What kind of housing is offered?
items.answer: Most assignments include furnished housing close to the facility or in town.

items.question: Can I apply if I’m from another province?
items.answer: Yes. We assist with licensing through CRNNL or CLPNNL.

items.question: Are northern travel assignments available?
items.answer: Yes. We staff coastal communities and northern Labrador placements regularly.

items.question: Is bilingualism required?
items.answer: No, but it is considered an asset in some communities.

items.question: Do I need prior experience to apply?
items.answer: Yes. Candidates must have at least 2 years of relevant healthcare experience to qualify for placements.

blocks.html: We help you navigate the provincial licensing process and reimburse licensing fees under select terms and conditions—so you can focus on getting started stress-free.
Travel RNs and LPNs in Newfoundland & Labrador must hold an active nursing license and up-to-date BLS certification. Make sure your documents are current and ready to upload.
All nurses are licensed through the College of Registered Nurses of Newfoundland and Labrador (CRNNL) and the College of Licensed Practical Nurses of Newfoundland and Labrador (CLPNNL).
You may also need to submit a vulnerable sector check, immunization records, and proof of insurance. Our team will guide you through every step.
Have questions about Newfoundland and Labrador nursing requirements? Our team can point you in the right direction and make sure you’re prepared for every step of the process.
